title: NASA Floods the Launch Pad With 450,000 Gallons to Stop Sound

scenes.text: Before liftoff, NASA floods the launch pad with hundreds of thousands of gallons of water.
It's not for fire. It's for sound.
The rocket's exhaust makes about one hundred seventy-six decibels at liftoff.
That can shake the rocket and its launcher apart.
So about twenty seconds before liftoff, the water starts to flow, at over a million gallons a minute.
It soaks up the sound energy of the exhaust. A flood, so a rocket doesn't shake itself apart.

description:
NASA's Artemis launch pad system dumped about 450,000 gallons of water in a 30-second test, at over a million gallons per minute at peak.
The water absorbs the sound energy of the exhaust so the rocket and launcher aren't damaged by pressure waves.
Did you know sound could do that?
first_comment: Have you ever heard a rocket launch in person?
